subject: Physics
body: A man of mass $60\ \text{kg}$ comes with velocity $v$ and jumps into a car of mass $120\ \text{kg}$ at rest. The combined velocity is $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Then $v$ is :
solution:
No external horizontal force acts on the man–car system, so linear momentum is conserved:

$$60\,v+120\times0=(60+120)\times2$$

$$60v=360\;\Rightarrow\;v=6\ \text{m/s}$$

subject: Physics
body: Two waves having wavelengths $4.08\ \text{m}$ and $4.16\ \text{m}$ produce $40$ beats in $12\ \text{s}$. Find the velocity of the waves in the medium.
solution:
Both waves travel with the same speed $v$, so their frequencies are $\dfrac{v}{\lambda_1}$ and $\dfrac{v}{\lambda_2}$. The beat frequency is the difference of the two frequencies:

$$\frac{v}{\lambda_1}-\frac{v}{\lambda_2}=\frac{40}{12}$$

$$v\left(\frac{1}{4.08}-\frac{1}{4.16}\right)=\frac{40}{12}\;\Rightarrow\;v\,\frac{4.16-4.08}{4.08\times4.16}=\frac{40}{12}$$

$$v\approx707\ \text{m/s}$$

subject: Physics
body: The work function of a metal is $6.63\times10^{-19}\ \text{J}$. Then the maximum wavelength of light that can remove photoelectrons is (in nm) :
solution:
The longest wavelength that can still emit photoelectrons is the threshold wavelength, where the photon energy just equals the work function and the maximum kinetic energy is zero:

$$\phi=\frac{hc}{\lambda}\;\Rightarrow\;\lambda=\frac{hc}{\phi}=\frac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{6.63\times10^{-19}}=3\times10^{-7}\ \text{m}$$

$$\lambda=300\ \text{nm}$$
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

subject: Physics
body: A drop of radius $2\ \text{cm}$ is broken into $64$ equal drops. Find the gain in surface energy. The surface tension of water is $0.075\ \text{N/m}$.
solution:
The volume stays the same, so for the radius $r$ of each small drop:

$$\frac43\pi(2\times10^{-2})^3=64\times\frac43\pi r^3\;\Rightarrow\;r=\frac{2\times10^{-2}}{4}=5\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}$$

The gain in surface energy is the surface tension times the increase in surface area:

$$\Delta E=T\left[64\times4\pi r^2-4\pi R^2\right]=0.075\times4\pi\left[64\times(5\times10^{-3})^2-(2\times10^{-2})^2\right]$$

$$\Delta E\approx1.13\times10^{-3}\ \text{J}=1.13\ \text{mJ}$$

subject: Physics
body:
Match the following quantities with their frequencies (given in the options in the same order) :

(i) Human voice lower hearing limit

(ii) High quality music

(iii) Earth wave

(iv) Radio wave
solution:
The lower limit of human hearing is $20\ \text{Hz}$, which rules out option (C), where it is given as $10\ \text{Hz}$.

High quality music is matched with $440\ \text{Hz}$, and the earth wave with $8\ \text{Hz}$. Options (C) and (D) give $40\ \text{Hz}$ and values of $4\ \text{Hz}$ and $2\ \text{Hz}$ here, so they do not fit.

Options (A) and (B) differ only in the range of radio waves. The answer key takes the radio wave range as $330\ \text{kHz}$ to $300\ \text{GHz}$, which is option (A).

subject: Physics
body: In a meter bridge, a resistance of $15\ \Omega$ is connected in the left gap and an unknown resistance $R$ in the right gap. The null point (balance point) is obtained at $45\ \text{cm}$ from the left end. Find the value of $R$.
solution:
At the null point of a meter bridge the resistances are in the ratio of the balancing lengths:

$$\frac{15}{R}=\frac{45}{100-45}$$

$$R=\frac{15\times55}{45}=\frac{55}{3}\ \Omega$$

subject: Physics
body: A block of mass $4m$ rests on a smooth ice slab. A horizontal force $2mg$ pulls it towards the left, and a light string attached to it passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the slab and carries a block of mass $m$ hanging vertically. If the tension in the string is $T=\dfrac{x}{5}\,mg$, find $x$.
solution:
The pull of $2mg$ drags the block $4m$ to the left, which lifts the hanging block $m$ upward with the same acceleration $a$.

For the hanging block $m$ (accelerating upward):

$$T-mg=ma$$

For the block $4m$ (accelerating towards the force):

$$2mg-T=4ma$$

Substituting $ma=T-mg$ in the second equation:

$$2mg-T=4(T-mg)\;\Rightarrow\;5T=6mg\;\Rightarrow\;T=\frac65\,mg$$

Hence $x=6$.

subject: Physics
body: The moment of inertia of a thin hollow sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its diameter (an axis through its centre) is :
solution:
For a thin hollow spherical shell, the moment of inertia about any axis through its centre (a diameter) is

$$I=\frac{2}{3}MR^2$$

For comparison, a solid sphere about a tangent has $\dfrac75MR^2$, a disc about a diameter has $\dfrac{MR^2}{4}$ and a ring about a diameter has $\dfrac{MR^2}{2}$; none of these equals $\dfrac{2MR^2}{3}$.

body:
For the following gate, the output $Y$ is given by :

![gate](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)
solution:
The symbol is an AND gate with a small circle (bubble) at its output, i.e. a NAND gate. Its output is the complement of the AND of the inputs:

$$Y=\overline{A\cdot B}$$

subject: Physics
body: A particle moves in the $x$–$y$ plane according to the rule $x=A\cos(\omega t)$, $y=A\sin(\omega t)$. The particle follows :

options.D: A straight-line path inclined equally to the $x$ and $y$ axes

solution:
Square the two equations and add:

$$\frac{x^2}{A^2}+\frac{y^2}{A^2}=\cos^2\omega t+\sin^2\omega t=1$$

$$x^2+y^2=A^2$$

This is the equation of a circle of radius $A$, so the particle follows a circular path.

subject: Physics
body: Charges are placed at three corners of a square of side $d$: a charge $\dfrac q2$ at the top-left corner, a charge $q$ at the bottom-left corner and a charge $\dfrac q2$ at the bottom-right corner. Find the electric field at the fourth corner $D$ (top-right).
solution:
The two charges $\dfrac q2$ are each at distance $d$ from $D$, so each produces a field

$$E_{q/2}=\frac{K(q/2)}{d^2}=\frac{Kq}{2d^2}$$

These two fields are perpendicular (one along the top edge, one along the right edge), so their resultant is

$$E_R=\sqrt{\left(\frac{Kq}{2d^2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{Kq}{2d^2}\right)^2}=\sqrt2\,\frac{Kq}{2d^2}$$

and it points along the diagonal, away from the corner holding $q$.

The charge $q$ is at the opposite corner, at distance $\sqrt2\,d$, and its field at $D$ points along the same diagonal:

$$E_q=\frac{Kq}{(\sqrt2d)^2}=\frac{Kq}{2d^2}$$

$$E_{total}=\left(\sqrt2+1\right)\frac{Kq}{2d^2}$$

subject: Physics
body: A uniform current is flowing along the length of an infinite, straight, thin, hollow cylinder of radius $R$. The magnetic field $B$ produced at a perpendicular distance $d$ from the axis of the cylinder is plotted in a graph. Which of the following figures looks like the plot ?
solution:
Apply Ampere's law to a circular loop of radius $d$ around the axis.

For $d<R$ the loop encloses no current (all the current is on the surface of the cylinder):

$$B\times2\pi d=\mu_0I_{in}=0\;\Rightarrow\;B=0$$

For $d>R$ the loop encloses the whole current $I$:

$$B\times2\pi d=\mu_0I\;\Rightarrow\;B=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi d}$$

So $B$ is zero inside, jumps to its maximum value at $d=R$ and then falls off as $1/d$. This is graph (C).

subject: Physics
body:
Read the assertion and reason carefully to mark the correct option out of the options given below.

Assertion : Dimensions of pressure $\times$ time is the same as that of the coefficient of viscosity.

Reason : Coefficient of viscosity $=\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Velocity gradient}}$

options.A: If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: If both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: If assertion is true, but reason is false.
options.D: If both the assertion and reason are false.

solution:
The coefficient of viscosity is defined by

$$\eta=\frac{F}{A\,\dfrac{dv}{dx}}$$

Its dimensions are

$$[\eta]=\frac{MLT^{-2}}{L^2\cdot T^{-1}}=[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$$

Pressure has dimensions $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$, so

$$[P]\times[T]=[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]=[\eta]$$

The assertion is true. The reason is false, because $\eta$ is the force per unit area divided by the velocity gradient; the given expression leaves out the area.

subject: Physics
body: A pendulum of length $250\ \text{cm}$ is released from rest when the string makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical. Find its maximum velocity. (Take $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.)
solution:
The speed is maximum at the lowest point. The bob falls through a height

$$h=\ell-\ell\cos60^\circ=2.5-1.25=1.25\ \text{m}$$

By conservation of energy:

$$mgh=\tfrac12mv^2\;\Rightarrow\;v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{2\times10\times1.25}=5\ \text{m/s}$$
topic: Conservative forces and conservation of energy

subject: Physics
body: If $\vec r=\left(3\hat i+\hat j\right)\ \text{m}$, $\vec v=\left(3\hat j-\hat k\right)\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, $m=1\ \text{kg}$ and $\left|\vec L\right|=\sqrt{x}\ \text{N m s}$, find the value of $x$.
solution:
The angular momentum is $\vec L=m\left(\vec r\times\vec v\right)$:

$$\vec L=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\3&1&0\\0&3&-1\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(-1-0)-\hat j(-3-0)+\hat k(9-0)$$

$$\vec L=-\hat i+3\hat j+9\hat k$$

$$|\vec L|=\sqrt{1^2+3^2+9^2}=\sqrt{91}\;\Rightarrow\;x=91$$

subject: Physics
body: The periods of two planets A and B are $T_A=2T_B$. Find the ratio of the radii of their revolution, $\dfrac{r_A}{r_B}$.
solution:
By Kepler's third law, $T^2\propto r^3$, so

$$\left(\frac{T_A}{T_B}\right)^2=\left(\frac{r_A}{r_B}\right)^3$$

$$\left(\frac{r_A}{r_B}\right)^3=2^2=4\;\Rightarrow\;\frac{r_A}{r_B}=4^{1/3}$$

subject: Physics
body:
Read the assertion and reason carefully to mark the correct option out of the options given below.

Assertion : The work done by $n$ moles of gas in an adiabatic process is $w=\dfrac{nR\left(T_2-T_1\right)}{1-\gamma}$

Reason : If work is done on a gas, then its temperature will increase.

options.A: If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: If both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: If assertion is true, but reason is false.
options.D: If both the assertion and reason are false.

solution:
For an adiabatic process, $PV^\gamma=\text{constant}$ and the work done by the gas is

$$w=\frac{P_2V_2-P_1V_1}{1-\gamma}=\frac{nR\left(T_2-T_1\right)}{1-\gamma}$$

so the assertion is true.

The reason is false as a general statement. Work done on a gas raises its temperature only if no heat escapes; in an isothermal compression, for example, the temperature stays constant because heat flows out.

subject: Physics
body: The resolving power of a telescope for an aperture of $24.4\ \text{cm}$ and a wavelength $\lambda=2440\ \text{\AA}$ is :
solution:
The limit of resolution of a telescope is $\Delta\theta=\dfrac{1.22\lambda}{a}$, and the resolving power is its reciprocal:

$$\text{R.P.}=\frac{a}{1.22\,\lambda}=\frac{24.4\times10^{-2}}{1.22\times2440\times10^{-10}}$$

$$\text{R.P.}\approx8.2\times10^{5}$$

subject: Physics
body: The centripetal acceleration of a particle moving on a circle of constant radius $r$ is given by $a_c=k^2rt^2$. Find the power delivered by the force acting on the particle.
solution:
The centripetal acceleration is $a_c=\dfrac{v^2}{r}$, so

$$\frac{v^2}{r}=k^2rt^2\;\Rightarrow\;v=krt$$

The tangential acceleration is

$$a_t=\frac{dv}{dt}=kr$$

so the tangential force is $F=ma_t=mkr$. Only this force changes the speed, so the power delivered is

$$P=Fv=(mkr)(krt)=mk^2r^2t$$

subject: Chemistry
body: Which of the following is not a copolymer?
solution:
Neoprene is a homopolymer. It is obtained from a single monomer, $2$-chlorobuta-$1,3$-diene (chloroprene).

Buna-S (styrene butadiene rubber) is a copolymer of buta-$1,3$-diene and styrene, and PHBV is a copolymer of $3$-hydroxybutanoic acid and $3$-hydroxypentanoic acid.
chapter: Polymers and Chemistry in Everyday Life

subject: Chemistry
body: The most stable lanthanide in the divalent form is :
solution:
The electronic configuration of europium is $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^76s^2$. On losing the two $6s$ electrons it forms $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$ with a half-filled, extra-stable $4f^7$ configuration.

So the $+2$ state is the most stable for Eu among the lanthanides.

subject: Chemistry
body: What is the product formed when a primary amine reacts with nitrous acid at room temperature?
solution:
A primary aliphatic amine reacts with nitrous acid (from $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$) to form a diazonium salt. Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable: they decompose at once, releasing nitrogen quantitatively and giving the alcohol.

$$\mathrm{R-NH_2+HNO_2\longrightarrow\left[R-\overset{+}{N_2}Cl^-\right]\xrightarrow{H_2O}ROH+N_2+HCl}$$

subject: Chemistry
body: Aniline is treated with $\mathrm{Br_2+H_2O}$, and then with $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$. The final product is :
solution:
Bromine water brominates aniline at all three activated positions (two ortho and one para) to give $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline.

$\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}$ converts the $\mathrm{NH_2}$ group into the diazonium salt, and hypophosphorous acid then replaces the diazonium group by hydrogen:

$$\mathrm{C_6H_2Br_3\overset{+}{N_2}Cl^-\xrightarrow{H_3PO_2}C_6H_3Br_3}$$

The product is $1,3,5$-tribromobenzene.

subject: Chemistry
body: The zeta potential is a property of colloidal particles related to their :

options.C: Charge on surface of the colloidal particle

solution:
The potential difference between the fixed layer and the diffused layer of opposite charges around a colloidal particle is called the zeta potential (or electrokinetic potential).

It is used to describe the preferential adsorption of ions on the particle, i.e. the electrical charge on the surface of the colloidal particles.

subject: Chemistry
body: The stability of the $\alpha$-helix structure of a protein is due to :
solution: In an $\alpha$-helix, the $\mathrm{C=O}$ group of each amino acid is hydrogen-bonded to the $\mathrm{N-H}$ group of the amino acid four residues ahead. These hydrogen bonds hold the coiled structure together.

subject: Chemistry
body: The hybridisation of P in $\mathrm{PF_5}$ is $sp^xd^y$. What is $y$ ?
solution:
Phosphorus in $\mathrm{PF_5}$ has five bond pairs and no lone pair, so it uses five hybrid orbitals: one $s$, three $p$ and one $d$.

The hybridisation is $sp^3d$, so $y=1$.

subject: Chemistry
body: Which of the following has the minimum synergic bonding?
solution:
Synergic bonding in metal carbonyls involves back-donation of electrons from filled metal $d$ orbitals into the empty $\pi^*$ orbitals of CO. The more $d$ electrons the metal (in oxidation state zero) has available, the stronger the back-bonding.

The metals have these numbers of $d$ electrons: $\mathrm{Mn}$ in $[\mathrm{Mn(CO)_5}]$ and $[\mathrm{Mn_2(CO)_{10}}]$: $d^7$; $\mathrm{Fe}$ in $[\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}]$: $d^8$; $\mathrm{Cr}$ in $[\mathrm{Cr(CO)_6}]$: $d^6$.

$[\mathrm{Cr(CO)_6}]$ has the fewest $d$ electrons, so it has the minimum synergic bonding.

subject: Chemistry
body: The purple colour obtained in Lassaigne's test for sulphur is due to the formation of :
solution:
In Lassaigne's test the sulphur of the organic compound is converted to sodium sulphide. With sodium nitroprusside it gives a violet (purple) colour:

$$\mathrm{Na_2S+Na_2[Fe(CN)_5NO]\longrightarrow Na_4[Fe(CN)_5NOS]}$$

This confirms the presence of sulphur.

body: The work function of a metal is $6.63\times10^{-19}\ \text{J}$. Find the maximum (threshold) wavelength of light required to emit a photoelectron.
solution:
At the threshold the kinetic energy of the emitted electron is zero, so the photon energy equals the work function:

$$\phi=\frac{hc}{\lambda}\;\Rightarrow\;\lambda=\frac{hc}{\phi}=\frac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^{8}}{6.63\times10^{-19}}=3\times10^{-7}\ \text{m}$$

$$\lambda=300\ \text{nm}$$

subject: Chemistry
body: Which of the following gives $\mathrm{N_2}$ on thermal decomposition?
solution:
Barium azide decomposes on heating to give nitrogen:

$$\mathrm{Ba(N_3)_2\xrightarrow{\Delta}Ba+3N_2}$$

Sodium nitrate gives $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$, and nitric acid decomposes to $\mathrm{NO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$, so neither gives $\mathrm{N_2}$.

subject: Chemistry
body:
In the given reaction, two molecules of benzaldehyde react with $\mathrm{NaOD}$ in $\mathrm{D_2O}$:

$$2\ \mathrm{PhCHO}\xrightarrow[\ \mathrm{D_2O}\ ]{\ \mathrm{NaOD}\ }x+\mathrm{Ph-COO^-}$$

$x$ is :
solution:
Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.

$\mathrm{OD^-}$ adds to the carbonyl group of one molecule. This intermediate transfers a hydride ion to the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule:

$$\mathrm{PhCHO+OD^-\longrightarrow PhCH(O^-)OD}\xrightarrow{\ \text{hydride transfer to PhCHO}\ }\mathrm{PhCOOD+PhCH_2O^-}$$

The acid then gives its deuteron to the alkoxide:

$$\mathrm{PhCOOD+PhCH_2O^-\longrightarrow PhCOO^-+PhCH_2OD}$$

So $x=\mathrm{Ph-CH_2-OD}$.

subject: Chemistry
body: $\mathrm{H_2+CuO\rightarrow}$ Product
solution:
Hydrogen is a good reducing agent. Passed over heated copper(II) oxide it reduces it to copper metal:

$$\mathrm{H_2+CuO\longrightarrow Cu+H_2O}$$

subject: Chemistry
body: Find the valence shell electronic configuration of the element present just above the element E of group $16$ and period $4$.
solution:
The element of group $16$ in period $4$ is selenium (Se). The element just above it in the group is sulphur.

The electronic configuration of sulphur is $[\mathrm{Ne}]3s^23p^4$, so its valence shell configuration is $3s^23p^4$.

subject: Chemistry
body: Calculate the amount of electricity needed to convert one mole of $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$.
solution:
The balanced half-reaction is

$$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}+14H^++6e^-\longrightarrow2Cr^{3+}+7H_2O}$$

so $6$ moles of electrons are needed per mole of dichromate.

$$Q=nF=6\times96500\ \text{C}=579000\ \text{C}$$

subject: Chemistry
body: Find the heat absorbed for an isothermal process in vacuum (expansion of a gas from $V_1=4\ \text{L}$ to $V_2=10\ \text{L}$).
solution:
In vacuum the external pressure is zero, so no work is done in the expansion: $w=0$.

For an isothermal process of an ideal gas, $\Delta U=0$. By the first law,

$$\Delta U=q+w\;\Rightarrow\;0=q+0\;\Rightarrow\;q=0$$

subject: Chemistry
body:
Assertion : For Group 15 elements, the acidity of the pentavalent oxide is greater than that of the trivalent oxide.

Reason : Down the group, acidity decreases.

options.A: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: Both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: Assertion is true, but reason is false.
options.D: Assertion is false, but reason is true.

solution:
An oxide of an element in a higher oxidation state is more acidic than that in a lower oxidation state, so the assertion is true.

The acidic character of the oxides also decreases down the group (the $\mathrm{E_2O_3}$ oxides of nitrogen and phosphorus are purely acidic, those of arsenic and antimony are amphoteric, and that of bismuth is predominantly basic), so the reason is true.

However, the trend down the group does not explain why the pentavalent oxide is more acidic than the trivalent oxide of the same element. So the reason is not the correct explanation.

subject: Chemistry
body:
The alkene shown below reacts with HBr. The major product is :

![structure](data:image/png;base64,)
solution:
HBr adds to the double bond according to Markovnikov's rule. The proton adds to the carbon that gives the more stable carbocation.

Adding $\mathrm{H^+}$ to the carbon farther from the ring gives a benzylic carbocation, which is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring. The bromide ion then attacks this carbocation.

So bromine ends up on the carbon attached to the ring, giving the product shown in (A), (1-bromopentyl)benzene.

subject: Chemistry
body:
Statement-1 : $[\mathrm{Ni(CN)_6}]^{4-}$ is square planar, $d^2sp^3$ and diamagnetic, whereas $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ is square planar, $sp^3$ hybridised and paramagnetic.

Statement-2 : $\mathrm{NiCl_4^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ have the same $d$ configuration, geometry and hybridisation.

options.A: Statement 1 and statement 2 both are correct.
options.B: Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is wrong.
options.C: Statement 1 is wrong but statement 2 is correct.
options.D: Statement 1 and statement 2 both are wrong.

solution:
Statement-1 is wrong. $d^2sp^3$ hybridisation gives an octahedral shape, not a square planar one. Also $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ is tetrahedral ($sp^3$) and diamagnetic, because Ni(0) has a $3d^{10}$ configuration, so it is neither square planar nor paramagnetic.

Statement-2 is wrong. $\mathrm{NiCl_4^{2-}}$ contains $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ($d^8$) and is tetrahedral, $sp^3$ and paramagnetic. $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ contains Ni(0) ($d^{10}$) and is diamagnetic. Both are tetrahedral and $sp^3$, but their $d$ configurations are different.

So both statements are wrong.

subject: Chemistry
body: $0.5\ \text{g}$ of a bromine-containing organic compound gives $0.40\ \text{g}$ of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. What is the percentage of bromine present in the organic compound? (Round off to the nearest integer.)
solution:
In $\mathrm{AgBr}$ (molar mass $188$), the mass fraction of bromine is $\dfrac{80}{188}$.

$$\%\ \text{of Br}=\frac{80}{188}\times\frac{\text{mass of AgBr}}{\text{mass of compound}}\times100=\frac{80}{188}\times\frac{0.40}{0.5}\times100$$

$$\%\ \text{of Br}\approx34.04\approx34$$

subject: Chemistry
body:
How many of the following are aromatic compounds?

![structure](data:image/png;base64,)
solution:
A compound is aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, completely conjugated and has $(4n+2)$ $\pi$ electrons (Huckel's rule).

(1) The cyclopentadienyl anion has $6$ $\pi$ electrons in a planar, fully conjugated ring. It is aromatic.

(2) The cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation has $6$ $\pi$ electrons in a planar, fully conjugated ring. It is aromatic.

(3) As drawn, the two ring-fusion carbons are $sp^3$ hybridised, so the $\pi$ system is not continuous around the rings. It is not aromatic.

(4) The cycloheptatrienyl anion has $8$ $\pi$ electrons, which is $4n$, so it is antiaromatic and not aromatic.

Hence only $2$ compounds are aromatic.

subject: Maths
body:
Two vertical poles $AB$ (of height $2h$) and $PQ$ (of height $h$) stand on level ground with $B$ and $Q$ at their feet, $160\ \text{m}$ apart. A point $O$ on $BQ$ is $80\ \text{m}$ from each pole. The angle of elevation of $P$ (the top of the pole $PQ$) from $O$ is $\dfrac\pi8$ and the angle of elevation of $A$ (the top of the pole $AB$) from $O$ is $\theta$.

Find $\tan^2\theta$.
solution:
From $O$, the pole $PQ$ gives

$$\tan\frac\pi8=\frac{h}{80}$$

and the pole $AB$ gives

$$\tan\theta=\frac{2h}{80}=2\tan\frac\pi8\;\Rightarrow\;\tan^2\theta=4\tan^2\frac\pi8$$

Using $\tan^2\dfrac\pi8=\dfrac{1-\cos\frac\pi4}{1+\cos\frac\pi4}$:

$$\tan^2\frac\pi8=\frac{1-\frac1{\sqrt2}}{1+\frac1{\sqrt2}}=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt2+1}=\left(\sqrt2-1\right)^2$$

$$\tan^2\theta=4\left(\sqrt2-1\right)^2=4\left(3-2\sqrt2\right)$$

subject: Maths
body: Find the probability that a three-digit number has at least two odd digits.
solution:
The total number of three-digit numbers is $9\times10\times10=900$.

All three digits odd: $5\times5\times5=125$.

Exactly two odd digits:

If the first digit is odd and exactly one of the other two is odd: $5\times2\times5\times5=250$.

If the first digit is even (non-zero) and the other two are odd: $4\times5\times5=100$.

So there are $350$ numbers with exactly two odd digits.

Favourable cases $=125+350=475$.

$$P=\frac{475}{900}=\frac{19}{36}$$

subject: Maths
body: Find the area of the region defined by $y^2\le8x$, $y\ge\sqrt{2x}$ and $x\le1$.
solution:
For $0\le x\le1$ the region lies between the upper branch of the parabola $y=\sqrt{8x}$ and the curve $y=\sqrt{2x}$ (both in the first quadrant).

$$\text{Area}=\int_0^1\left(\sqrt{8x}-\sqrt{2x}\right)dx=\int_0^1\left(2\sqrt2-\sqrt2\right)\sqrt x\,dx=\sqrt2\int_0^1\sqrt x\,dx$$

$$\text{Area}=\sqrt2\cdot\frac23\left[x^{3/2}\right]_0^1=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}$$

subject: Maths
body:
Let $y=y(x)$ satisfy the differential equation

$$x\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2-y^2}}+e^{y/x}\right)\frac{dy}{dx}=x+y\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2-y^2}}+e^{y/x}\right)$$

such that $y(1)=0$. If $y(2\alpha)=\alpha$, find $\alpha$.
solution:
Put $y=vx$, so that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$. The bracket becomes $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-v^2}}+e^v$. Writing it as $A$:

$$xA\left(v+x\frac{dv}{dx}\right)=x+vxA\;\Rightarrow\;x\,A\,\frac{dv}{dx}=1$$

$$\int\left(\frac1{\sqrt{1-v^2}}+e^v\right)dv=\int\frac{dx}{x}$$

$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac yx\right)+e^{y/x}=\ln x+c$$

Using $y(1)=0$: $0+1=0+c$, so $c=1$.

Now $y(2\alpha)=\alpha$ means $x=2\alpha$ and $\dfrac yx=\dfrac12$:

$$\sin^{-1}\frac12+e^{1/2}=\ln(2\alpha)+1\;\Rightarrow\;\frac\pi6+\sqrt e-1=\ln(2\alpha)$$

$$2\alpha=e^{\frac\pi6+\sqrt e-1}\;\Rightarrow\;\alpha=\frac12\,e^{\frac\pi6+\sqrt e-1}$$

subject: Maths
body: For the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, the eccentricity is $e=\sqrt{\dfrac52}$ and the length of the latus rectum is $6\sqrt2$. If $y=2x+c$ is a tangent to the hyperbola, find $c$.
solution:
From the eccentricity:

$$e^2=1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}=\frac52\;\Rightarrow\;b^2=\frac32a^2$$

The length of the latus rectum is $\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=6\sqrt2$:

$$\frac{2\cdot\frac32a^2}{a}=3a=6\sqrt2\;\Rightarrow\;a=2\sqrt2,\quad a^2=8,\quad b^2=12$$

The line $y=mx+c$ touches the hyperbola when $c^2=a^2m^2-b^2$. Here $m=2$:

$$c^2=8\times4-12=20\;\Rightarrow\;c=\pm2\sqrt5$$

subject: Maths
body: The circle $(x-1)^2+(y-2)^2=5$ meets the $x$-axis at $A(0,0)$ and $B(2,0)$. Tangents are drawn to the circle at $A$ and $B$, and they intersect at the point $C$. Find the area of the triangle $ABC$.
solution:
The chord $AB$ lies on the $x$-axis, so $AB=2$.

The point $C$ is the pole of the chord $AB$ with respect to the circle. The tangent at $A(0,0)$ is

$$(0-1)(x-1)+(0-2)(y-2)=5\;\Rightarrow\;x+2y=0$$

and the tangent at $B(2,0)$ is

$$(2-1)(x-1)+(0-2)(y-2)=5\;\Rightarrow\;x-2y=2$$

Solving the two equations gives $C\left(1,-\dfrac12\right)$.

The height of $C$ above the chord $AB$ (the $x$-axis) is $\dfrac12$, so

$$\text{Area}=\frac12\times AB\times\frac12=\frac12\times2\times\frac12=\frac12$$

body: Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix with $|A|=2$. Find $\left|\,|A|\,\mathrm{adj}\left(5\,\mathrm{adj}\,A^3\right)\right|$.
solution:
For an $n\times n$ matrix $B$, $|kB|=k^n|B|$ and $|\mathrm{adj}\,B|=|B|^{n-1}$. Here $n=3$.

First, $|A^3|=|A|^3$ and $|\mathrm{adj}\,A^3|=|A^3|^2=|A|^6$.

Then

$$|5\,\mathrm{adj}\,A^3|=5^3\,|\mathrm{adj}\,A^3|=5^3|A|^6$$

$$|\mathrm{adj}\left(5\,\mathrm{adj}\,A^3\right)|=|5\,\mathrm{adj}\,A^3|^2=5^6|A|^{12}$$

Finally, multiplying the matrix by the scalar $|A|$ multiplies its determinant by $|A|^3$:

$$\left|\,|A|\,\mathrm{adj}\left(5\,\mathrm{adj}\,A^3\right)\right|=|A|^3\cdot5^6|A|^{12}=|A|^{15}\cdot5^6=2^{15}\cdot5^6$$

$$2^{15}\cdot5^6=2^9\times10^6=512\times10^6=512000000$$

body: Let $\vec a=2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec b=3\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec c=c_1\hat i+c_2\hat j+c_3\hat k$. If $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are coplanar, $\vec a\cdot\vec c=5$ and $\vec b$ is perpendicular to $\vec c$, find $122\left(c_1+c_2+c_3\right)$.
solution:
The three conditions give three equations.

$\vec a\cdot\vec c=5$:

$$2c_1+c_2+3c_3=5\qquad(1)$$

$\vec b\perp\vec c$:

$$3c_1+3c_2+c_3=0\qquad(2)$$

Coplanar vectors have zero scalar triple product:

$$\begin{vmatrix}c_1&c_2&c_3\\2&1&3\\3&3&1\end{vmatrix}=c_1(1-9)-c_2(2-9)+c_3(6-3)=0$$

$$-8c_1+7c_2+3c_3=0\qquad(3)$$

From (2), $c_3=-3c_1-3c_2$. Substituting in (1) and (3):

$$-7c_1-8c_2=5,\qquad-17c_1-2c_2=0$$

The second gives $c_2=-\dfrac{17}{2}c_1$, and then $-7c_1+68c_1=5$, so

$$c_1=\frac{10}{122},\quad c_2=-\frac{85}{122},\quad c_3=\frac{225}{122}$$

$$122\left(c_1+c_2+c_3\right)=10-85+225=150$$

subject: Maths
body: Find the number of five-digit numbers divisible by $6$ that can be formed using the digits $3,6,1,7,2,5$ without repetition.
solution:
A number is divisible by $6$ if it is divisible by both $2$ and $3$. So its last digit must be even, and the sum of its digits must be a multiple of $3$.

The six digits add up to $3+6+1+7+2+5=24$. A five-digit number omits one digit, and the remaining sum must be a multiple of $3$. Omitting $6$ gives $18$ and omitting $3$ gives $21$. Omitting any other digit gives $23$, $17$, $22$ or $19$, which do not work.

Omit $6$: the digits are $3,1,7,2,5$. The last digit must be $2$, and the other four can be arranged in $4!=24$ ways.

Omit $3$: the digits are $6,1,7,2,5$. The last digit can be $6$ or $2$, so there are $2\times4!=48$ ways.

Total $=24+48=72$.

subject: Maths
body: Find the number of real solutions of $4x^7+3x^3+5x+1=0$.
solution:
Let $f(x)=4x^7+3x^3+5x+1$.

$$f'(x)=28x^6+9x^2+5>0\quad\text{for all real }x$$

So $f$ is strictly increasing and can cross the $x$-axis at most once.

Since $f(-1)=-4-3-5+1=-11<0$ and $f(0)=1>0$, it does cross the axis.

Hence the equation has exactly $1$ real solution.

body: Let $(a_n)$ be a G.P. such that $a_1\times a_3\times a_5\times a_7=\dfrac{1}{1296}$ and $a_2+a_4=\dfrac{7}{36}$. Then find $a_6+a_8+a_{10}$.
solution:
Let the first term be $a$ and the common ratio $r$.

$$a_1a_3a_5a_7=a\cdot ar^2\cdot ar^4\cdot ar^6=a^4r^{12}=\left(ar^3\right)^4=\frac1{1296}\;\Rightarrow\;ar^3=\pm\frac16$$

Also $a_2+a_4=ar+ar^3=\dfrac7{36}$.

If $ar^3=-\dfrac16$, then $ar=\dfrac{13}{36}$ and $r^2=\dfrac{ar^3}{ar}<0$, which is impossible. So $ar^3=\dfrac16$ and

$$ar=\frac7{36}-\frac16=\frac1{36}\;\Rightarrow\;r^2=\frac{1/6}{1/36}=6$$

$$a_6+a_8+a_{10}=ar^5+ar^7+ar^9=ar\left(r^4+r^6+r^8\right)=\frac1{36}\left(36+216+1296\right)=43$$

subject: Maths
body: The mean and variance of $15$ observations are $8$ and $3$ respectively. One observation was wrongly taken as $5$ in place of $20$. Find the correct variance.
solution:
From the wrong data, $\sum x=15\times8=120$, and

$$3=\frac{\sum x^2}{15}-8^2\;\Rightarrow\;\sum x^2=15\times67=1005$$

Correct the values by removing $5$ and adding $20$:

$$\sum x=120-5+20=135,\qquad\sum x^2=1005-5^2+20^2=1380$$

$$\text{Variance}=\frac{1380}{15}-\left(\frac{135}{15}\right)^2=92-81=11$$
